Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Keratinocyte carcinoma (KC) treatment is guided primarily by tumor characteristics, but sociodemographic factors may also influence care. We examined associations of age, sex, marital status, and educational level with treatment selection. Methods: Adults with actinic keratosis or KC were recruited in four Belgian and Dutch settings between 2020 and September 2023. Treatment was categorized as topical/non-invasive therapy, Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS), or standard surgical excision (reference). Multinomial regression adjusted for histologic group, tumor size, location, recruiting center, and an age-independent Charlson comorbidity component. The primary analysis included 681 participants, with additional sensitivity analyses. Results: The model converged normally. Age (global p = 0.023) and educational level (p = 0.002) were associated with treatment selection; sex and marital status were not. Each additional decade of age was associated with lower odds of MMS versus standard excision (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.755, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.595-0.959). Low versus high education was associated with lower odds of topical/non-invasive treatment versus standard excision (aOR 0.123, 95% CI 0.034-0.450), but not with MMS (aOR 0.533, 95% CI 0.232-1.222). Conclusions: Age and educational level were associated with KC treatment selection after clinical and center adjustment. These associations do not establish inequitable care because relevant patient-, clinician-, and pathway-level determinants were not captured.

item.title: Local and systemic inflammatory and immune pathways in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: emerging therapeutic targets.
item.dc:creator: Ceruti D, van Houten P, Changoer P, Netea MG, Jaeger M, Netea-Maier RT
item.description:
Authors: Ceruti D, van Houten P, Changoer P, Netea MG, Jaeger M, Netea-Maier RT
Journal: Cancer treatment reviews | DOI: 10.1016/j.ctrv.2026.103240
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 43019925



Abstract:
Anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC) is a rare endocrine cancer and one of the most lethal malignancies with only few treatment options. Most patients present with advanced and unresectable disease, and the median survival is approximately three months. In recent years, systemic treatments have become available for a subgroup of patients with ATC harboring targetable variants, such as BRAF/MEK inhibitors for patients with pathogenetic BRAFV600E variants. However, only a small proportion of patients with ATC are eligible for these treatments, and most treated patients develop resistant and progressive disease. Hence, an urgent need remains for new treatment approaches. Accumulating evidence underlines the roles of systemic inflammation, immunosuppressive and protumoral immune cells tumor infiltration, and elevated numbers of circulating proinflammatory myeloid immune cells in tumor angiogenesis, metastasis, and disease progression of ATC. In this review, we highlight recent advances in understanding the pathogenesis of ATC and summarize latest trends in systemic treatments for patients with ATC. Moreover, based on these developments in understanding the pathophysiology of the disease, we propose how targeting different protumoral processes could lead to future treatment modalities for patients with ATC, with a specific focus on inflammatory processes and the innate immune system.

item.title: Treatment hotspots and controversies in papillary thyroid microcarcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yu L, Liu F, Wang F, Yuan S, Zhao X, Gu S, Guo R, Zhao J, Zhang W
item.description:
Authors: Yu L, Liu F, Wang F, Yuan S, Zhao X, Gu S, Guo R, Zhao J, Zhang W
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag216
Published: 2026-Nov-05
PMID: 43010779



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The significant global rise in the detection rate of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC) has sparked intense debates concerning overdiagnosis and overtreatment. Consequently, therapeutic strategies are shifting from radical surgery toward risk-stratified management, including active surveillance (AS) and minimally invasive techniques (MIT). Core controversies focus on the necessity of surgical intervention, the extent of prophylactic central neck dissection, and selection criteria for MIT versus conventional surgery. METHODS: This review systematically evaluates the comparative evidence on AS, thermal ablation (TA), and surgical treatment for PTMC, highlighting divergent Eastern and Western management philosophies to provide an optimized framework for clinical decision-making. RESULTS: Although AS demonstrates favorable survival benefits and health economic advantages for patients with PTMC, unresolved clinical risks persist. Notably, Chinese guidelines adopt stricter standards compared to the international 10 mm threshold. Among MIT, TA exhibits well-established short-term efficacy; however, recent expert consensus emphasizes a strict therapeutic hierarchy to prevent misuse, given the paucity of long-term recurrence data. CONCLUSION: An individualized framework based on risk stratification is essential for PTMC management, balancing oncological safety and quality of life.

item.title: Transcript Abundance of IL6, CXCL9, LIF and LIFR in Glottic Lesions: Relationship to Histology and to Narrow-Band Imaging Vascular Patterns.
item.dc:creator: Barańska M, Borkowska E, Pietruszewska W
item.description:
Authors: Barańska M, Borkowska E, Pietruszewska W
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213545
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 43026866



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Narrow-band imaging (NBI) is an established adjunct in laryngeal lesion assessment, but the molecular processes underlying high-risk vascular patterns are poorly defined. We compared IL6, CXCL9, LIF, and LIFR transcript abundance between glottic carcinoma and non-cancerous lesions, related it to NBI patterns, and tested whether IL6 adds diagnostic information to NBI. METHODS: In this prospective single-center exploratory study, 62 patients operated on for glottic lesions (33 squamous cell carcinomas, 29 non-cancerous lesions) underwent preoperative NBI (European Laryngological Society and Ni classifications); transcripts were quantified by RT-qPCR. RESULTS: IL6 was higher in carcinoma (median 5.97 vs. 0.30; p = 0.004), also with non-detects set to the detection limit (p = 0.001) and among ever-smokers only (p = 0.0008). Sex adjustment attenuated the association (OR 1.78 per 10-fold increase, 95% CI 0.98-3.23; p = 0.06); smoking could not be adjusted for, as all carcinomas occurred in ever-smokers. CXCL9, LIF, and LIFR did not differ. Adding IL6 to NBI did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC 0.00-0.02; bootstrap 95% CIs including zero). Within non-cancerous lesions, IL6 was nominally higher in high-risk NBI patterns (n = 5-7), but no stratified comparison survived false-discovery-rate correction. CONCLUSIONS: IL6 transcript abundance was higher in glottic carcinoma, but the difference was sensitive to sex adjustment and, when measured in bulk tissue, may reflect lesion composition, including inflammatory infiltrate. IL6 showed no evidence of diagnostic value beyond NBI, and its link with vascular morphology remains a hypothesis.

item.title: Real-World Outcomes of Oral VEGFR Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Containing Therapy in Unresectable Malignant Mesothelioma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
item.dc:creator: Liu Z, Zhong J, Wan R, Duan JC, Wang ZJ, Bai H, Wang J
item.description:
Authors: Liu Z, Zhong J, Wan R, Duan JC, Wang ZJ, Bai H, Wang J
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213541
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 43026862



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic treatment choices after failure of standard therapy are limited for malignant mesothelioma. Oral vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (VEGFR-TKIs) have been incorporated into salvage treatment strategies, but real-world evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety remains scarce. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a single-center cohort comprising patients with pathologically confirmed malignant mesothelioma treated at Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences/National Cancer Center between 1 April 2017 and 16 March 2023. Patients with unresectable disease who received a VEGFR-TKI-containing regimen and had sufficient clinical follow-up for outcome assessment were included. Progression-free survival (PFS) served as the primary endpoint. Objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS) from VEGFR-TKI initiation, and recorded adverse events were included as secondary endpoints. RESULTS: The cohort comprised 48 patients, with a median follow-up of 24.0 months. The Kaplan-Meier estimated median PFS was 4.8 months (95% CI, 2.9-8.8), and median OS from VEGFR-TKI initiation was 17.9 months (95% CI, 13.5-not estimable). Among 39 response-evaluable patients, 6 achieved partial response, 20 had stable disease, and 13 had progressive disease as their best overall response, yielding an ORR of 15.4% and a DCR of 66.7%. Two patients remained progression-free for more than 24 months. Grade 3 adverse events in the records included hematuria, hypertension, and nausea/vomiting; no grade 4 or grade 5 adverse event was documented. CONCLUSIONS: VEGFR-TKI-containing therapy was associated with clinically relevant disease control in unresectable malignant mesothelioma, with durable benefit observed in a small subset of patients. These observations warrant further evaluation of VEGFR-TKI-based salvage strategies in larger multicenter cohorts.

item.title: Targeted alpha therapy for solid tumors: biological rationale, clinical advances, and future perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Li Q, Xie J, Chen F, Li L, Yang C
item.description:
Authors: Li Q, Xie J, Chen F, Li L, Yang C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.2007300
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041765



Abstract:
Targeted alpha therapy (TAT) delivers high-linear-energy-transfer radiation over a few cell diameters and is being explored for resistant and microscopic solid-tumor disease. This targeted narrative review evaluates alpha-emitting platforms and clinical evidence by tumor type and development stage, with a focused literature update through 12 October 2026. Unlike broader radiochemistry-centered reviews, we place approved, randomized, early-phase, observational, and preclinical findings in separate evidence tiers. Radium-223 dichloride has randomized survival evidence in symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, whereas molecularly targeted actinium-225, lead-212, astatine-211, and thorium-227 agents remain investigational in the indications discussed. Updated examples include the 2026 ACTION-1 actinium-225-DOTATATE dosimetry substudy, the 2026 first-in-human astatine-211-MABG study, 2025 lead-212-DOTAMTATE phase II disclosures, and a negative 2025 mesothelin-targeted thorium-227 study. Quantitative outcomes are reported with their study design and limitations rather than interpreted as indirect head-to-head comparisons. Major barriers include isotope supply, incomplete daughter retention, salivary, marrow, and kidney toxicity, spatially heterogeneous target uptake, and uncertainty in patient-specific microdosimetry. We propose practical, imaging-led selection and a priority-ranked translational roadmap.

item.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging: a mini review of current applications and future directions.
item.dc:creator: Lotfian G, Ginat DT
item.description:
Authors: Lotfian G, Ginat DT
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.2010320
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041688



Abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to enhance medical imaging in pediatric oncology through quantitative image analysis and clinical decision support. This mini review examines the emerging role of AI in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging, including applications in lesion detection and characterization, tumor segmentation and volumetric analysis, treatment planning, longitudinal surveillance, prognostication, and precision medicine. Particular attention is given to the challenges of translating these approaches to pediatric populations, where rare and heterogeneous tumors, limited datasets, variable imaging protocols, and insufficient multicenter validation remain important barriers. We also discuss emerging strategies that may facilitate clinical translation, including federated learning, multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and integration with existing radiology workflows. Although pediatric-specific evidence remains limited, continued multicenter collaboration and prospective validation may enable AI-based tools to provide more reproducible quantitative imaging assessment and increasingly personalized clinical decision support. Ultimately, the clinical value of these technologies will depend on their ability to augment radiologist expertise and improve patient care through responsible integration into routine practice.

item.title: Long-term outcomes of globe-sparing surgery combined with adjuvant radiotherapy for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhao SX, Xu WQ, Zhao XH, Su D, Li YY, Ma R, Hei Y, Mu XT, Yang XJ
item.description:
Authors: Zhao SX, Xu WQ, Zhao XH, Su D, Li YY, Ma R, Hei Y, Mu XT, Yang XJ
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1934640
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041427



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term outcomes of radiotherapy after globe-sparing surgery for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) and compare different radiotherapy protocols. METHODS: This retrospective comparative case series included 97 patients with LGACC treated with globe-sparing surgery followed by postoperative radiotherapy between November 2003 and April 2023. Patients received one of four protocols differing in clinical target volume (CTV) expansion and radiation dose. Primary outcomes included locoregional recurrence, distant metastasis, locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), progression-free survival, and overall survival. RESULTS: The median age was 38 years, and median follow-up was 7.2 years. The overall 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates were 80.2%, 74.5%, and 74.5%, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified R2 resection (HR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.53‑11.35, P = 0.005), cribriform histology (HR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.08‑0.81, P = 0.020), and smaller CTV expansion (≤0.5 cm; HR = 4.06, 95% CI: 1.41‑11.67, P = 0.009) as independent predictors of local recurrence. Patients treated with ≤0.5-cm CTV expansion and ≤54 Gy had significantly lower 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates (55.2%, 40.5%, and 40.5%) than those treated with 1-cm CTV expansion and 60-80 Gy (90.5%, 90.5%, and 90.5%; P < 0.001). DMFS did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.599). Best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20-20/40 was preserved in 35.1% of patients. The 5-year risk of radiation retinopathy was 25.1% and 43.6% (P = 0.057) in the no extended-margin and extended-margin groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Radiotherapy with 1-cm CTV expansion and a dose of 60 Gy after globe-sparing surgery provided favorable locoregional control for LGACC. Distant metastasis remained the predominant cause of treatment failure.

item.title: TMSB10 marks a malignant epithelial programme spatially associated with fibroblast-matrix niches in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yao B, Tang Y, Liu S, Nie X, Lin L, Xu Q
item.description:
Authors: Yao B, Tang Y, Liu S, Nie X, Lin L, Xu Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1969309
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041408



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant epithelial states at the tumour-stroma interface may contribute to local invasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but their reproducibility across patients and spatial relationship with fibroblast-matrix niches remain unclear. METHODS: Single-cell transcriptomes from 16 untreated OSCC samples were analysed to localise TMSB10 and derive a TMSB10-associated invasion-related programme (TIP) through within-patient comparisons of aneuploid epithelial cells. Frozen TIP scores were evaluated in independent single-cell and spatial cohorts. Spatial associations were tested using adjusted generalised additive models and random-effects meta-analysis. Survival associations were examined in GSE41613 and TCGA-HNSC, and TMSB10 was silenced in HN6 and HN30 cells. RESULTS: Among 89, 323 cells, TMSB10 was highly expressed in epithelial and endothelial compartments. TMSB10-high aneuploid epithelial cells exhibited 1, 569 differentially expressed genes and enrichment of 16 Hallmark pathways related to proliferation, oxidative metabolism, and epithelial plasticity. Frozen TIP scores showed concordant directions across patients and in GSE103322. TIP-core and TIP-anchor were positively associated with cancer-associated fibroblast/extracellular matrix (CAF/ECM) scores in all 18 spatial sections, with pooled effects of 0.1434 and 0.1456, respectively (both FDR = 0.000402); this association was reproduced in all four GSE220978 patients. In GSE41613, higher TMSB10 expression was associated with poorer overall and disease-specific survival after clinical adjustment, whereas TCGA-HNSC showed no consistent adjusted association. TMSB10 knockdown reduced CCK-8 signals, wound closure, and Transwell migration in both cell lines. CONCLUSION: Within malignant epithelial cells, TMSB10 expression is associated with a reproducible, pEMT-related programme spatially associated with CAF/ECM-rich regions. Knockdown findings support the involvement of TMSB10 in OSCC cell growth and migration.

item.title: Access to Care and Practice Variation in the Assessment of Ankyloglossia.
item.dc:creator: Hunter MO, Lee K, Sanchez RE, Kistler I, Elmaraghy CA, Manning AM, Pattisapu P, Chiang T, Miller AL
item.description:
Authors: Hunter MO, Lee K, Sanchez RE, Kistler I, Elmaraghy CA, Manning AM, Pattisapu P, Chiang T, Miller AL
Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.43915
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 43024236



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Diagnosis and treatment of ankyloglossia has increased in recent years. A lack of universal evaluation and management guidelines may contribute to inconsistent practice patterns and variable access to care. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate access to care and practice pattern variation in the treatment of ankyloglossia as a source of breastfeeding difficulty across clinicians and sites of care in Ohio. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study of pediatric dentists and pediatric and general otolaryngologists providing treatment to pediatric patients in Ohio was conducted using a secret shopper approach from October 6, 2025, to January 5, 2026. All pediatric dentists and otolaryngologists providing treatment to pediatric patients were eligible for inclusion. Health care professionals were identified using lists obtained from the Ohio State Dental Board and the American Academy of Otolaryngology. EXPOSURE: Clinics were contacted via phone by a simulated patient's mother using a vignette describing a 2-week-old infant with breastfeeding difficulty characterized by painful latch and inquiring regarding ankyloglossia (ie, tongue tie) evaluation. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were time to first available appointment and procedure cost to patient on the day of service. Secondary outcomes included referral requirement, potential for same-day procedures, procedure technique, additional procedures discussed during scheduling, insurance acceptance, and total cost of consultation and procedure. RESULTS: A total of 175 clinics representing 487 health care professionals (299 dentists and 188 otolaryngologists) were contacted. The median (IQR) appointment wait time was 14 (7-28) days. For practices providing cost information, time-of-service cash payment was required by 31 of 36 dental offices (86%), while all otolaryngology practices (38 of 38; [100%]) billed medical insurance. Dental clinics were more likely to empirically recommend other procedures (eg, maxillary frenulum release) at the time of appointment scheduling (29 of 45 [64%]) than otolaryngology offices (1 of 38 [3%]) (P < .001). Across all practices, the median (IQR) cost of lingual frenotomy alone was $474 ($350-$545), while total cost (consultation and all recommended procedures) ranged from $200 to $1515. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study of pediatric dental and otolaryngology clinics in Ohio, access to care for ankyloglossia was similar, but the anticipated cost of procedures varied widely, as did empiric recommendations for intervention beyond lingual frenotomy. Prospective patients should be aware of this heterogeneity and the potential for significant price differences for treatment.

item.title: RESOLVE-IPD: Individual Patient Data Reconstruction and Uncertainty-Aware Subgroup Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Lang L, Zhao Y, Gao Q, Xu Y
item.description:
Authors: Lang L, Zhao Y, Gao Q, Xu Y
Journal: JCO precision oncology | DOI: 10.1200/PO-26-00267
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 43024845



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Individual patient data (IPD) from oncology trials are essential for reliable evidence synthesis but are rarely publicly available, necessitating reconstruction from published Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves. Existing reconstruction methods can be affected by digitization errors, strong uniform censoring assumptions, and the inability to recover subgroup-level pseudo-IPD when only aggregate statistics are available. We developed RESOLVE-IPD, a computational framework that combines vector-based KM extraction, censoring-informed survival reconstruction, and uncertainty-aware subgroup recovery for pseudo-IPD reconstruction and subgroup meta-analysis. METHODS: RESOLVE-IPD transforms published survival data into reconstructed pseudo-IPD. The framework uses VEC-KM for vector-graphic coordinate extraction and CEN-KM to incorporate censoring marks and reported risk tables into overall-population reconstruction. To address subgroup evidence recovery, we introduced MAPLE, an algorithm that identifies an ensemble of plausible subgroup labelings consistent with reported aggregate summaries. RESOLVE-IPD enables downstream IPD-based evaluations, including subgroup meta-analyses that quantify and propagate uncertainty inherent in the reconstruction process. RESULTS: RESOLVE-IPD was demonstrated through subgroup meta-analyses of four trials in advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, focusing on patients with low programmed death-ligand 1 expression and patients age ≥65 years. VEC-KM and CEN-KM reconstructed overall survival pseudo-IPD that closely reproduced published KM curves and reported summary statistics. MAPLE produced plausible subgroup reconstructions consistent with reported hazard ratios and survival estimates. Uncertainty-propagating meta-analysis generated pooled survival and interval-specific hazard-ratio estimates while preserving subgroup reconstruction uncertainty. CONCLUSION: RESOLVE-IPD provides a framework for reconstructing overall and subgroup pseudo-IPD from published survival information and for propagating reconstruction uncertainty, thereby supporting more robust and transparent secondary evidence synthesis in precision oncology.

item.title: Molecular Profiling for Precision Medicine in Adrenocortical Carcinoma: Real-World Data From the French Network ENDOCAN-COMETE.
item.dc:creator: Lemaire S, Marret G, Moog S, Jannin A, Haissaguerre M, Lugat A, Sajous C, Laboureau S, Eas F, Lassolle H, et al.
item.description:

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare tumor with poor prognosis. Precision medicine and molecularly matched treatment (MMT) represent a new opportunity in oncology. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of patients with advanced ACC within the French ENDOCAN COMETE network from 2009 to 2022 who have been providing access to molecular profiling (MP). We investigated the benefits of the MMT strategy in terms of response according to RECIST, median progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and growth modulation index (GMI). RESULTS: We enrolled 78 patients with ACC who underwent MP of the primary tumor in 41 patients. Most patients had metastasis at diagnosis, with at least one GRAS criterion. P53 alteration and activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway were the most frequent genetic alterations. No mutations were found in 20.5% of patients' tumors. The microsatellite instability phenotype was present in two cases. The median OS from the date of first metastasis was 33.3 months (95% CI, 24.7 to 56.2) with most patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy and mitotane as first-line therapy. Twelve patients were treated with MMT as a second- or third-line therapy. An objective response rate was observed in two patients with a complete response under immunotherapy. The median PFS with MMT was 2.5 months. The mean GMI was 1.02, above 1.3 in three patients (4%). CONCLUSION: Molecular alteration-based precision medicine is associated with potential antitumor benefits in a limited subset of patients with ACC.

item.title: ACP3 Theranostics in Prostate Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Luo Z, Chen D, Ma T, Zeng P, Li X, Shi H, Hu Z
item.description:
Authors: Luo Z, Chen D, Ma T, Zeng P, Li X, Shi H, Hu Z
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213511
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 43026833



Abstract:
Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) and radioligand therapy have established a major clinical paradigm for prostate cancer theranostics. Their performance is influenced by interpatient and interlesional heterogeneity, treatment-related changes in PSMA expression, and physiological ligand uptake in organs such as the salivary glands and kidneys, creating a rationale for complementary targets with different lesion coverage and normal-tissue distribution. ACP3 (acid phosphatase 3; historical symbol ACPP) encodes prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP), which is also termed prostate-specific acid phosphatase (PSAP) in older pathology literature. PAP has served as a serum biomarker, an immunohistochemical marker of prostatic origin, and an immunotherapeutic antigen. DNA-encoded library screening identified the high-affinity PAP ligand OncoACP3, and the resulting [177Lu]Lu-OncoACP3-DOTAGA radioligand and OncoACP3-GlyPro-MMAE small-molecule drug conjugate achieved target-dependent payload delivery and antitumor activity in preclinical models. First-in-human PET and subsequent pharmacokinetic and diagnostic dosimetry studies of [68Ga]Ga-OncoACP3-DOTA demonstrated visualization of localized and metastatic prostate cancer lesions and a normal-organ distribution distinct from that of PSMA-targeted ligands. This narrative review synthesizes the molecular characteristics and biological functions of PAP, historical clinical applications, and modern ACP3-targeted imaging and therapeutic platforms. Existing studies now provide a biological foundation, preclinical proof of targeted payload delivery, and early human imaging, pharmacokinetic, and diagnostic-dosimetry evidence. Prospective development should next define the ligand-accessible PAP pool, imaging-positivity criteria, therapeutic dosimetry, and the patient groups in whom ACP3 adds value to the PSMA theranostic framework.

item.title: Is the Duration of Antibiotic Prophylaxis Associated With Severe Surgical Site Infection, Length of Hospital Stay, and Hospitalization Charges After Cleft Lip and/or Palate Surgery?

item.description:

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite widespread antibiotic prophylaxis in cleft lip and/or palate surgery, the frequency of severe surgical site infection (SSI) requiring debridement or reoperation and the optimal duration of prophylaxis remain uncertain. Large-scale, real-world evidence is needed to better inform antibiotic prophylaxis strategies in this population. PURPOSE: To estimate the frequency of severe SSI and measure the association between antibiotic prophylaxis duration and postoperative outcomes across cleft lip and/or palate procedures. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This nationwide, multicenter, retrospective cohort study used the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination inpatient database (April 2012 to March 2022). Patients undergoing cleft lip and/or palate surgery were screened, and those with immunocompromised status, preoperative antibiotic use, or no antibiotic prophylaxis were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: Duration of postoperative antibiotic prophylaxis (short term: ≤ 2 days vs prolonged: ≥ 3 days). MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE(S): The primary outcome was the frequency of severe SSI, defined as SSI requiring debridement or reoperation during the same hospitalization. The secondary outcomes were length of hospital stay and hospitalization charges. COVARIATES: Age, sex, body mass index, anesthesia duration, procedure category, comorbidities at admission, and teaching hospital status. ANALYSES: Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate associations between prophylaxis duration and outcomes. Subgroup analyses were performed for the 4 surgical procedure groups. The frequency of severe SSI was summarized descriptively. A P value < .05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Of 17,005 patients screened, 13,333 subjects were analyzed: 6,172 (46.3%) received short-term prophylaxis, and 7,161 (53.7%) received prolonged prophylaxis. The mean (SD) age was 6.5 (9.0) years, and 7,199 (54.0%) were male. Severe SSI occurred in one subject in the prolonged group (overall frequency, 0.008%). Short-term prophylaxis was associated with a 0.5-day shorter hospital stay (95% CI: -0.8 to -0.2; P = .001) but not with hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference, -53 US dollars [95% CI: -168 to 62]; P = .4). These findings were consistent across the 4 procedure groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Severe SSI requiring debridement or reoperation was extremely rare in both groups. Short-term antibiotic prophylaxis was associated with shorter hospital stays but not with hospitalization charges.

item.title: Hospital Price Transparency in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.

item.description:
Authors: Wang TT, Liang L, Peacock Z, Lee C
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.014
Published: 2026-Oct-30

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Hospital Price Transparency Rule requires hospitals to publish prices for medical and surgical services, but reporting is often incomplete. For patients paying out of pocket, discounted cash prices are particularly relevant, yet their availability for oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS) procedures is unknown. PURPOSE: To evaluate the availability of 3 price types for common OMS procedures, including discounted cash prices, insurer-negotiated rates, and gross charges, and identify factors associated with discounted cash price availability. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This cross-sectional study used the Turquoise Health Price Transparency Dataset. Hospitals reporting a price for at least one of 9 elective OMS procedures were included. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor was a set of factors including billing class (facility fee, professional fee), specific procedure and procedure domain (dental extraction, implant/ridge augmentation, orthognathic, temporomandibular joint, and benign pathology), and U.S. Census region. MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE: The primary outcome was discounted cash price availability, defined as whether a discounted cash price was reported for a hospital procedure combination. Secondary outcomes were insurer-negotiated rate availability and gross charge availability. COVARIATES: None. ANALYSES: Descriptive statistics summarized availability of the 3 price types. Associations between predictors and discounted cash price availability were evaluated using χ2 tests and multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < .001. RESULTS: Of 7,319 hospitals, 2,717 (37.1%) reported a price for at least one selected OMS procedure. Across the 9 procedures, 95.1% of hospitals reported an insurer-negotiated rate, 21.8% a discounted cash price, and 21.0% a gross charge. When stratified by billing class, discounted cash prices were available for 7.7% of facility fees compared with 30.4% of professional fees (P < .001). In adjusted analysis, the odds that a discounted cash price was reported were lower for dental extraction (odds ratio (OR), 0.39; 95% CI, 0.24 to 0.63) and implant/ridge augmentation (OR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.16 to 0.56) procedures compared to orthognathic procedures, and nearly 6 times greater for professional compared to facility fees (OR, 5.98; 95% CI, 4.58 to 7.81; all P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Despite widespread availability of insurer-negotiated rates, discounted cash prices were uncommon, particularly for dental services. This may limit cost information for patients paying out of pocket.

item.title: Clinical and CT body-composition model for major pathological response to neoadjuvant tislelizumab, albumin-bound paclitaxel, and nedaplatin in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Xu H, Zheng W, Chen S, Wu S
item.description:
Authors: Xu H, Zheng W, Chen S, Wu S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1859690
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43031628



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia and osteoporosis are linked to poor treatment outcomes and are significantly underdiagnosed in esophageal cancer patients. Despite the promising efficacy of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NACI) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), predicting treatment response remains a major clinical hurdle. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the associations of sarcopenia and osteoporosis on pathological response and to develop a both clinical and computed tomography (CT)-based predictive model for NACI outcomes in ESCC patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted in 179 patients with ESCC who underwent radical resection after neoadjuvant tislelizumab, albumin-bound paclitaxel, and nedaplatin. Within each of 500 stratified bootstrap resamples, five-fold cross-validation was used to determine the optimal LASSO penalty parameter, followed by Firth logistic regression. Aggregated out-of-bag predictions underwent five-fold cross-fitted recalibration. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using the AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Major pathological response (MPR) rates were 70.0%, 40.0%, 22.0%, and 8.3% in the control, osteoporosis-only, sarcopenia-only, and osteosarcopenia groups, respectively. In multivariable Firth logistic regression, lower tumor grading, absence of comorbidities, absence of lymphovascular invasion, absence of sarcopenia, and a higher intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) area percentage were associated with a greater likelihood of achieving MPR, whereas osteoporosis was not associated with MPR (P = 0.130). The cross-fitted recalibrated model achieved an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI, 0.835-0.934), with 0.818 accuracy, 0.840 sensitivity, and 0.800 specificity at a threshold of 0.405. Calibration was satisfactory (Brier score, 0.136; intercept, -0.009; slope, 0.960; Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.219), and decision curve analysis showed clinical net benefit across thresholds of 0.08-0.80. CONCLUSION: Absence of sarcopenia and a higher IMAT area percentage were associated with a greater likelihood of achieving major pathological response. The combined clinical and CT-based model showed good internally validated performance.

item.title: Sequencing-informed, patient-specific droplet digital PCR assays for circulating tumor DNA monitoring in recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer: a pilot study.
item.dc:creator: Amodio LL, Grossmann L, Gächter S, Nowak M, Schaufelberger M, Mennicke C, Rahmani-Khajouei S, Zoche M, Moch H, Weber A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Amodio LL, Grossmann L, Gächter S, Nowak M, Schaufelberger M, Mennicke C, Rahmani-Khajouei S, Zoche M, Moch H, Weber A, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1984504
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43031620



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC), early identification of treatment response remains challenging because imaging may be delayed or confounded by treatment-related changes and atypical response patterns under immunotherapy. Serial circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis may provide a minimally invasive measure of tumor dynamics and complement conventional imaging. We therefore investigated the feasibility and clinical relevance of patient-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR)-based ctDNA monitoring. METHODS: Nine patients with R/M HNSCC underwent tumor genomic profiling using FoundationOne® CDx as part of routine clinical care. Patient-specific single-nucleotide variants, including pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and technically suitable variants of uncertain significance, were selected for ddPCR assay development. Plasma samples were collected before and/or during systemic treatment, and ctDNA kinetics were assessed in relation to radiologic response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Sixteen single-target ddPCR assays were successfully established and combined into ten patient-specific single- or multi-target assay configurations. A total of 21 plasma samples were analyzed, and technically valid measurements were obtained for all samples. Pretreatment plasma was available for seven patients, of whom three (42.9%) had detectable ctDNA. Across all time points, ctDNA was detected at least once in six of nine patients (66.7%). Among the six patients with serial sampling, ctDNA kinetics showed descriptive agreement with radiologic assessment in five (83.3%). The single patient with increasing ctDNA developed progressive disease, whereas decreasing or stable ctDNA was accompanied by partial response or stable disease in four patients; one patient showed a mixed radiologic response. In an exploratory descriptive comparison, the single patient with increasing ctDNA had shorter observed PFS and OS than the five patients with decreasing or stable ctDNA levels. Given the group size of one patient, this observation is hypothesis-generating and does not establish a prognostic association. CONCLUSIONS: Patient-specific ddPCR-based ctDNA monitoring was technically feasible and showed agreement with radiologic assessment in most evaluable patients. These proof-of-concept findings support prospective evaluation of patient-specific ddPCR as a focused approach for longitudinal monitoring in R/M HNSCC; its comparative clinical utility and cost-effectiveness remain to be established.

item.title: A pretreatment TNM-metabolic vulnerability score with EBV DNA adjustment for risk stratification in non-metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Zhong J, Zhou C, Yi Q, Zhong K, Chen Z, Ouyang X, Xu C, Liao J, Chen W, Zhang X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1914286

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: TNM stage and pretreatment plasma Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA are central to risk assessment in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but they do not fully capture host metabolic reserve. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 160 patients with non-metastatic NPC treated from 2013 to 2022. The integrated metabolic vulnerability score (IMVS; range, 0-3) assigned 1 point each for stage IVA, triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio <1.217, and body mass index <23.79 kg/m2. Cox regression and bootstrap internal validation evaluated progression-free survival (PFS), with EBV DNA included as an adjustment variable. A broader 271-patient cohort from the same institution was used only for internal sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Thirty-three PFS events occurred in the modeling cohort. Five-year PFS was 100.0%, 91.9%, 72.1%, and 50.0% for IMVS scores 0, 1, 2, and 3, respectively. IMVS remained associated with PFS after adjustment for EBV DNA status (HR, 2.74; bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 1.89-4.75; P<0.001), although EBV DNA status itself was not independently significant in this cohort. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.715 for stage IVA, THR, and BMI and 0.727 after adding EBV DNA. In the broader same-institution cohort, the association persisted but was attenuated (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.14-2.10; P = 0.005). CONCLUSION: IMVS is an exploratory, low-cost risk-stratification tool that may complement, rather than replace, TNM stage and plasma EBV DNA. Prospective external validation and recalibration of the data-derived thresholds are required before clinical use.

item.title: Synchronous Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma in Non-Invasive Follicular Thyroid Neoplasm with Papillary-like Nuclear Features (NIFTP): Prevalence, Pathological Profile, and Limits of Pre-Operative Risk Prediction in a Multicentre Cohort.
item.dc:creator: Dobrinja C, Mastronardi M, Bernardi S, Bonati E, Bononi M, Calò PG, Canu GL, Cappellacci F, Chiofalo MG, Pasquale L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Dobrinja C, Mastronardi M, Bernardi S, Bonati E, Bononi M, Calò PG, Canu GL, Cappellacci F, Chiofalo MG, Pasquale L, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213505
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43026826



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP) was reclassified as a non-malignant entity in 2016 to reduce overtreatment. A proportion of NIFTP-containing glands nonetheless harbour a synchronous differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC). We quantified its prevalence and pathological profile and assessed whether routinely collected pre-operative variables identify affected patients. Methods: A multicentre retrospective cohort of 1185 adults with NIFTP confirmed at second histological review, operated on between 2017 and 2023 in 22 centres. The outcome was a synchronous DTC in the surgical specimen. A weighted random forest and an elastic-net logistic regression based on 13 pre-operative predictors were evaluated with 20-times repeated five-fold cross-validation, with all data-driven steps nested within training folds, and with leave-one-centre-out and temporal validation. Results: A synchronous DTC was present in 61 patients (5.1%; 95% CI 4.0-6.6; 6.2% after review of the stored reports), with marked between-centre variation (none recorded in eight centres). Fifty-eight carcinomas (95%) were pT1a; none had gross extra-thyroidal extension or nodal metastasis (nodes examined in 27 patients), and none met the 2025 American Thyroid Association criteria mandating a more extensive operation. No pre-operative variable differed between groups after multiplicity adjustment. The cross-validated AUROC was 0.56 (95% CI 0.47-0.65) for the random forest and 0.58 (0.48-0.67) for the elastic net; the within-centre concordance was 0.48 and the temporal-validation AUROC 0.39, and decision-curve analysis showed no net benefit over default strategies. Conclusions: About one in twenty NIFTP-containing specimens harbours a synchronous DTC, usually a low-risk papillary microcarcinoma. Routinely available pre-operative variables do not identify these patients; management should be guided by the pathology of the carcinoma itself.

item.title: Tumour Cell-Associated Heterogeneity in Antiviral Immunity Shapes Influenza Responses and Immune-Modulatory Signalling in Lung Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Miles MA, Rosano I, Liong S, Logan JM, O'Leary JJ, Brooks DA, Selemidis S
item.description:
Authors: Miles MA, Rosano I, Liong S, Logan JM, O'Leary JJ, Brooks DA, Selemidis S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213502
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43026823



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Respiratory viral infections occur within the same anatomical niche as lung cancer, yet how lung cancer cells respond to infection and how these responses influence antiviral and inflammatory signalling remain poorly understood. This study investigated innate immune responses to influenza A virus (IAV) infection across a panel of lung epithelial cell lines. METHODS: Non-malignant bronchial epithelial and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines representing adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma were infected with IAV. Antiviral and inflammatory gene expression, viral RNA and protein detection, infection-induced cell death, pattern recognition receptor expression, and immune checkpoint ligand expression were assessed using molecular, biochemical and flow cytometric approaches. Interferon (IFN) receptor blockade and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species scavenging were used to investigate selected signalling mechanisms. RESULTS: NSCLC cell lines exhibited heterogeneous innate immune responses to IAV infection, with differential regulation of RNA-sensing pathways and canonical antiviral signalling components. Although IFN responses were retained, NSCLC cells exhibited reduced infection-induced apoptosis and prolonged viral RNA and protein detection compared with non-malignant epithelial cells. IAV infection was also associated with changes in DNA-sensing receptor expression, including TLR9, and increased expression of the immune checkpoint ligand PD-L1. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify substantial cell line-associated heterogeneity in antiviral responses to IAV across lung epithelial cell lines, including NSCLC cells. The observed differences in viral RNA and protein detection, cell death responses and immune-modulatory signalling provide a framework for understanding how respiratory viral infections may interact with lung cancer cells to shape antiviral and inflammatory responses within the tumour environment.

item.title: Real-World Activity and Safety of Metronomic Cyclophosphamide in Advanced Soft-Tissue Sarcoma: The Multicenter MeRCY Study.
item.dc:creator: Bolognini C, Falcoz A, Simon P, Calcagno F, Hervieu A, Isambert N, Desmoulins I, Causeret S, Thibouw D, Kalbacher E, et al.
item.description:

Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Metronomic cyclophosphamide (MCP) is sometimes used for advanced soft-tissue sarcoma (STS) when standard therapies are unsuitable. We assessed its activity and safety in routine practice. Methods: This French three-center retrospective study included 60 adults with unresectable or metastatic STS who started MCP in 2008-2021. Patients received oral cyclophosphamide 50 mg twice daily on days 1-7 of 14-day cycles; 12 (20%) also received prednisolone during treatment weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Results: Median age was 70 years; 55% had ECOG performance status 2-3. Median PFS and overall survival (OS) were 2.6 months (95% CI, 1.8-3.6) and 6.4 months (95% CI, 4.2-9.3), respectively. The objective response rate was 5.0% (3/60; exact 95% CI, 1.0-13.9%) and the disease control rate was 21.7% (13/60; exact 95% CI, 12.1-34.2%); ten patients (16.7%) were not radiologically evaluable. In 21 patients aged >65 years treated in the first- or second-line setting, median PFS and OS were 3.2 and 7.7 months. Treatment-related adverse events were documented in 16 patients (26.7%), with no grade ≥3 events recorded. Conclusions: Intermittent low-dose MCP showed limited antitumor activity but favorable clinician-documented short-term tolerability in this multicenter cohort. Alongside prospective evidence, the results do not support routine use in unselected patients. MCP may retain an individualized palliative role when established systemic therapy is unsuitable.

item.title: Temporal Patterns of Patient-Reported Symptoms, Jaw Function, Oral Parafunctions, and Psychological Outcomes After Orthognathic Surgery in Skeletal Class III Patients.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dentofacial deformities can affect jaw function, oral health-related quality of life, and psychological well-being. Longitudinal evidence assessing multiple patient-reported outcomes remains limited. PURPOSE: To measure temporal changes in 6 patient-reported outcomes following bimaxillary orthognathic surgery. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, AND SAMPLE: This prospective longitudinal cohort study included consecutive adults with skeletal Class III dentofacial deformity who underwent bimaxillary surgery at Ondokuz Mayıs University between October 2024 and June 2025 and were followed for 6 months postoperatively. Patients with skeletal Class I or II deformity, clinically significant facial asymmetry requiring additional procedures, revision surgery, or American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II or higher were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor was assessment time: 1 week preoperatively (T0), and 6 weeks (T1), 3 months (T2), and 6 months (T3) postoperatively. OUTCOME VARIABLES: Outcomes were Fonseca Anamnestic Index (FAI), 8-item Jaw Functional Limitation Scale (JFLS-8), Oral Behaviors Checklist (OBC), 14-item Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14), 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) scale, and 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) scores. Lower scores indicate less symptom burden (FAI), functional limitation (JFLS-8), oral behavior frequency (OBC), adverse oral health impact (OHIP-14), anxiety symptom severity (GAD-7), or depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9). No single primary outcome was prespecified. COVARIATES: Age and sex. ANALYSES: Friedman tests and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (P < .0083) evaluated temporal changes. Secondary generalized estimating equation models adjusted for age and sex. RESULTS: All 37 participants completed follow-up (mean age, 20.9 ± 2.3 years; 26 female [70.3%]). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Patient-reported symptom burden, jaw functional limitation, oral behaviors, and adverse oral health impacts were lower at 6 months than at baseline, whereas psychological changes were less consistent. These temporal associations do not establish causal effects of surgery.

item.title: Extent of lymphadenectomy dictates adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in primarily resected esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a multi-cohort validation.
item.dc:creator: Huang Y, Lin X, Lin Y, Han Z
item.description:
Authors: Huang Y, Lin X, Lin Y, Han Z
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1920549
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43022032



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While primary surgery remains a crucial treatment for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), the uniform application of postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for pathologically node-positive patients exposes many to severe systemic toxicity. This study hypothesizes the existence of a specific lymph node dissection (LND) threshold that stratifies the survival benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy and aims to define this cutpoint to enable safe therapeutic de-escalation. METHODS: We conducted a multi-cohort retrospective study using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (n = 753, training cohort) and a Chinese single-center repository (n = 447, validation cohort) of patients with ESCC who underwent primary radical esophagectomy without radiotherapy. The optimal prognostic cutpoint for LND was mathematically determined using X-tile software. An interactive Cox proportional hazards nomogram incorporating an LND-by-chemotherapy interaction term was developed and validated. Subsequently, layer-specific 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed within separate surgical strata of the validation cohort to assess chemotherapy efficacy. RESULTS: X-tile analysis established 21 lymph nodes as the optimal LND threshold. Multivariable analysis confirmed that adequate LND (≥ 21 nodes) and adjuvant chemotherapy were independent protective prognostic factors. The interactive nomogram demonstrated good discrimination and calibration across both populations. Crucially, layer-specific PSM in the external validation cohort revealed divergent therapeutic responses dependent on surgical quality. For patients with suboptimal LND (< 21 nodes), adjuvant chemotherapy provided a significant survival benefit over surgery alone (P = 0.048). In contrast, for patients achieving an adequate LND (≥21 nodes), the addition of adjuvant chemotherapy yielded no further survival advantage (P = 0.085). CONCLUSIONS: Achieving the removal of ≥ 21 lymph nodes serves as a robust anatomical biomarker that fundamentally alters the postoperative therapeutic landscape for ESCC. Patients with suboptimal LND require adjuvant chemotherapy to compensate for potential residual disease, whereas those achieving the 21-node clearance threshold derive no additional survival benefit from systemic interventions and can be safely exempted from cytotoxic over-treatment.

item.title: Immunosenescence and Inflammaging in the Pathogenesis of Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Mihalj M, Mioč NF, Sabljić I, Čeprnja ZŠ, Tokić S, Buljan M
item.description:
Authors: Mihalj M, Mioč NF, Sabljić I, Čeprnja ZŠ, Tokić S, Buljan M
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213481
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 43026802



Abstract:
Non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy worldwide, and its incidence rises disproportionately with age. While cumulative ultraviolet (UV) exposure is the dominant recognised risk factor, it does not fully account for the steep age-associated increase in NMSC, suggesting that additional, underrecognised mechanisms operate in older skin. This review synthesises evidence that immune senescence (the age-related remodelling of innate and adaptive immunity) is a central and partly modifiable driver of NMSC aetiopathogenesis. We first outline the classical risk factors and the epidemiological and economic burden of NMSC, and revisit the proposal to regard recurrent NMSC as a chronic disease. We then examine four interlocking, age-associated processes: the accumulation of senescent cells and their pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype ("inflammaging") in the skin microenvironment; UV-induced suppression of cutaneous immune function; age-related dysbiosis of the skin microbiome and its impact on antitumour immunity; and the systemic decline of T-cell-mediated tumour immunosurveillance. We integrate these processes into a framework in which immune senescence contributes to the progression of accumulated cutaneous damage to overt malignancy, and consider the implications for prevention (including senotherapeutics, microbiome modulation, and immune-stratified surveillance) that extend beyond UV-directed measures alone.

item.title: A Literature-Derived Muscle Wasting-Related Prognostic Signature Identifies ZBTB7C as a Candidate Associated with Tumor-Related Skeletal Muscle Alterations in Esophageal Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Li Y, Xie C, Chen R, Ming Z, Huang H, Ding S
item.description:
Authors: Li Y, Xie C, Chen R, Ming Z, Huang H, Ding S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213479
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 43026800



Abstract:
Background: Skeletal muscle wasting is a frequent systemic complication of esophageal cancer and is associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes. However, the relationships among tumor-associated molecular characteristics, patient prognosis, and skeletal muscle alterations remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify prognostically relevant genes from a literature-curated muscle wasting-related gene set and investigate the potential association of ZBTB7C with tumor-related skeletal muscle alterations in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Methods: Transcriptomic and survival data from the complete TCGA-ESCA cohort and the independent GSE53625 cohort were analyzed using a predefined set of genes implicated in muscle wasting-related biology. Differential expression analysis, consensus clustering, Cox regression, LASSO-Cox analysis, survival analysis, functional enrichment, and immune-related analyses were performed. A six-gene prognostic signature was constructed in the TCGA cohort and externally evaluated in GSE53625. ZBTB7C was subsequently investigated using human ESCC tissues and cell lines, Zbtb7c-overexpressing AKR cells, AKR-conditioned medium-treated C2C12 myotubes, and an immunocompetent AKR/C57BL/6 syngeneic tumor model. Results: A total of 32 literature-curated muscle wasting-related genes were retained for analysis. A six-gene prognostic signature comprising ZBTB7C, DDIT3, RNF157, AMOTL1, TTLL12, and PDLIM2 was associated with overall survival, although its discriminatory performance was limited in the external validation cohort. ZBTB7C expression was reduced in ESCC tissues and cell lines, and higher expression was associated with favorable survival. Zbtb7c overexpression reduced PCNA expression in AKR tumor cells. Conditioned medium from Zbtb7c-overexpressing AKR cells attenuated MuRF-1 and Atrogin-1 expression, partially restored AKT, FOXO3A, and P70S6K phosphorylation, and increased global protein synthesis in C2C12 myotubes. In vivo, Zbtb7c overexpression suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by preservation of gastrocnemius muscle mass, attenuation of muscle protein homeostasis-related alterations, and a smaller decline in all-limb grip strength. Conclusions: These findings identify ZBTB7C as an exploratory candidate associated with esophageal cancer prognosis and tumor-related skeletal muscle alterations. However, its muscle-related effects cannot be fully distinguished from reduced tumor burden, and further mechanistic and clinical validation is required before its potential utility as a biomarker or therapeutic target can be established.

item.title: Factors Associated with Level II and V Involvement in Lateral Neck Dissection for pN1b Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Díaz Ríos P, Bustos Merlo AB, Arcelus Martínez JI, Becerra Massare A, Muñoz Pérez NV, Villar Del Moral JM

Abstract:
Background: Lateral neck dissection is the standard surgical treatment for patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and lateral cervical lymph node metastases (pN1b). However, the optimal extent of dissection remains debated, particularly for levels II and V. We examined patterns of nodal involvement and factors associated with metastases at these levels. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 70 patients with pN1b PTC who underwent lateral neck dissection between 2019 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and pathological variables were analyzed. The lymph node ratio (LNR), defined as metastatic nodes divided by harvested nodes, was dichotomized at the cohort median. Bivariate associations were assessed using Pearson's χ2 test, Fisher's exact test, or the Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test, as appropriate; p < 0.05 indicated statistical significance. Results: Median age was 46 years and 60% were female. Involvement was highest at levels III (82.9%) and IV (65.7%), followed by II (55.7%) and V (23.9%). Median LNR was 0.25. Level II involvement was more frequent in male patients (71.4% vs. 45.2%; p = 0.031) and patients with high versus low LNR (76.5% vs. 36.1%; p = 0.001). Histological subtype was associated with level V involvement (p = 0.027), predominantly in classic PTC. Conclusions: Male sex and higher LNR were associated with level II involvement in bivariate analyses; an exploratory association was also observed between histological subtype and level V involvement. These findings do not establish independent predictors or justify altering the extent of neck dissection. Larger cohorts and multivariable analyses should validate these findings.

item.title: Malignant transformation of an intracranial epidermoid cyst into squamous cell carcinoma: a case report and systematic review.
item.dc:creator: Onzere LE, Ma J, Stephano EE, Kisangai PM, Li Y, Quan W, Wu Y
item.description:
Authors: Onzere LE, Ma J, Stephano EE, Kisangai PM, Li Y, Quan W, Wu Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1978480
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43016707



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intracranial epidermoid cysts (IECs) are rare, benign congenital lesions that occasionally undergo malignant transformation into squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). This study presents a rare case of an IEC in the anterior cranial fossa transforming into SCC and reviews existing literature to summarize clinical characteristics, treatment strategies, and survival outcomes. METHODS: We detail the clinical presentation, management and long-term follow-up of a 52-year-old female who developed SCC 75 months after initial subtotal resection of an anterior cranial fossa IEC. We also conducted a comprehensive systematic literature search across PubMed, MEDLINE and CNKI in accordance with PRISMA guidelines compiling 59 well-documented cases (including our index case) to analyze demographic features, transformation intervals, treatment modalities and overall survival. RESULTS: Our patient underwent repeat subtotal tumor resection followed by adjuvant intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT). She maintained a disease-free survival (DFS) of 14 months post-radiotherapy (17 months post-reoperation) until July 2026, when she developed multifocal intraventricular recurrence. The literature review revealed a mean patient age of 54.7 years with an equal gender distribution (1.03:1). The cerebellopontine angle (CPA) was the most frequent tumor site (50.85%). The mean interval from IEC diagnosis to malignant transformation was 9.24 years. Prognosis for transformed SCC remains poor, with a median overall survival of 6 months. However, patients treated with surgery combined with radiotherapy demonstrated significantly improved outcomes (median survival 13 months) compared to those undergoing surgery alone (41 days). CONCLUSIONS: Malignant transformation of IECs into SCC is a rare, aggressive complication. Long-term surveillance with contrast-enhanced MRI is vital for patients with previously resected IECs. Early detection, maximal safe surgical resection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy currently offers the most favorable survival benefit.

item.title: Development and validation of a magnetic resonance imaging-based model for the prediction of progression-free survival before initial treatment of hypopharyngeal cancer treated with chemoradiation.
item.dc:creator: Tao H, Wei J, Zheng Q, Yang X, Sun Y
item.description:
Authors: Tao H, Wei J, Zheng Q, Yang X, Sun Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1928542
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43016519



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a radiomics-clinical model for prediction of the progression-free survival (PFS) in hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPSCC) patients treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: One hundred and thirteen patients with hypopharyngeal cancers treated by CCRT were enrolled and randomly divided into training (N = 80) and validation (N = 33) groups. Python's PyRadiomics toolkit was used to extract radiomic features from magnetic resonance diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) sequences, which included four categories: shape (14), first-order (230), texture (306), and wavelet (738). All feature preprocessing steps-including normalization, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) filtering, Pearson correlation filtering, and feature selection-were performed exclusively within the training set, with the same preprocessing parameters subsequently applied to the validation set. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized Cox regression algorithm with ten-fold cross-validation was used to screen key radiomic features and construct the Rad-score. We used Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank tests to assess the ability of the radiomic signature to stratify PFS risk, and constructed a radiomics nomogram to predict individual PFS probabilities at 1 and 2 years. RESULTS: The radiomics model consisting of six important features performed well in classifying patients into high- and low-risk groups of progression in both the training and test groups (log-rank test, p = 0.006 in the training cohort; p = 0.023 in the validation cohort, using the cutoff value of 0.025 determined from the training set). Age and T stage were chosen as clinically important variables based on univariate Cox regression analysis (p < 0.05). The radiomics nomogram demonstrated good differentiation ability, with C-indices of 0.904 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.816-0.992) and 0.858 (95% CI, 0.690-1.000) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. The time-dependent AUCs for predicting 1-year and 2-year PFS were 0.867 and 0.837, respectively, in the training cohort, and 0.737 and 0.715 in the validation cohort. CONCLUSION: The multiparametric DWI-based radiomics model may serve as a potential tool to predict PFS in patients with HPSCC treated with CCRT after further prospective validation.

item.title: DAMPs and NETs in Thyroid Diseases: Biological, Diagnostic, and Translational Perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Waczyński K, Choromańska B, Maciejczyk M, Lewoc-Magnuszewska M, Tkaczuk A, Grymuza J, Dadan J, Myśliwiec P
item.description:
Authors: Waczyński K, Choromańska B, Maciejczyk M, Lewoc-Magnuszewska M, Tkaczuk A, Grymuza J, Dadan J, Myśliwiec P
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213469
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 43026790



Abstract:
Thyroid diseases encompass a broad spectrum of autoimmune, inflammatory, and neoplastic disorders, yet current diagnostic approaches provide limited insight into innate immune activation and tumor-associated inflammatory remodeling. Damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as interconnected mediators of sterile inflammation with potential relevance to thyroid carcinogenesis, disease progression, and biomarker development. This narrative review synthesized literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus to evaluate the biological, diagnostic, and translational significance of DAMP- and NET-associated pathways in thyroid diseases, with particular emphasis on thyroid cancer. DAMPs such as high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), S100A8/A9, serum amyloid A, heat shock proteins, and extracellular nucleic acids may sustain inflammatory signaling through pattern-recognition receptors and contribute to tumor proliferation, angiogenesis, immune modulation, and therapeutic resistance. In parallel, circulating analytes associated with NET biology-including nonspecific cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and nucleosomes, pathway-associated citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), and composite myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA) complexes-have shown associations with thyroid malignancy, dedifferentiated disease, metastatic presentation, and greater disease severity. Experimental data further suggest that aggressive thyroid cancer cells, particularly anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, can induce extracellular trap formation and exploit neutrophil-derived signals to support tumor growth. However, limited disease specificity, assay heterogeneity, and the predominance of small or exploratory cohorts currently restrict clinical implementation. Future strategies should prioritize standardized, prospective validation of multimarker panels integrating DAMP- and NET-related analytes with imaging, cytology, molecular diagnostics, and clinicopathological risk stratification to determine whether they provide incremental value for diagnosis, prognostication, and longitudinal monitoring in thyroid cancer.

item.title: Temporal Associations Between Thyroid Cancer Epidemiological Trends and Classification Revisions.
item.dc:creator: Trovato M, Pandiyan B, Ferrari SM, Famà F, Benvenga S
item.description:
Authors: Trovato M, Pandiyan B, Ferrari SM, Famà F, Benvenga S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213468
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 43026789



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated potential temporal associations between international histopathological classifications, staging updates, and the long-term divergence observed between papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) and follicular thyroid cancer (FTC) incidence trends. Applying an advanced statistical protocol comprising the recursive Supremum Chow Test, Piecewise Segmented Regression with Regime Switching (PSR-RS), and a non-linear Markov-Switching Intercept and Slope (MSIA) model, we analyzed population-level annual incidence rates (AIR) in the United States from 1975 to 2023. METHODS: We implemented a two-pronged approach to identify and validate structural trend changes in incidence trends. Approach 1 tracked endogenous, data-driven incidence shifts, while Approach 2 tested the fixed calendar milestones corresponding to the official publication dates of major classifications. Crucially, this multistage analytical protocol was applied directly to the individual PTC and FTC series, as well as to the scale-independent log ratio, ln(PTC/FTC) and aggregate diagnostic gap timelines. RESULTS: The results show that the incidence gap between the two cancers widened until 2014 and stabilized thereafter. AG quadrupled from 2.9 per 100,000 population in 1975 (PTC AIR = 3.6 minus FTC AIR = 0.7) to 11.6 in 2014 (PTC AIR = 12.8 minus FTC AIR = 1.2) with no further increase thereafter (AG = 11.6 in 2022 and 2023). Under Approach 1, the natural breakpoints partitioned the timelines into highly diverse behavioral segments. Specifically, the data identified five evolutionary regimes for PTC, three independent regimes for FTC, and four distinct regimes for AG. The breakpoint identified in 1987 coincided with the staging updates introduced that year and marked a clear change in the incidence trends of both histotypes. Between 1987 and 1991, PTC incidence increased, while FTC incidence declined toward its historical minimum. Despite these changes, the aggregate diagnostic gap continued along its existing trend, with no structural break detected. The 2004 WHO third edition corresponded to a systematic upward level shift (β2 = +4.1500) associated with the formal codification of microcarcinomas. Finally, both analytical approaches converged on 2014 as a significant historical turning point in the slowing of incidence growth. This phase is characterized by a significant negative slope change (Δβ = -0.35) consistent with conservative classification updates and subsequent stabilization at a structural plateau. CONCLUSIONS: The progressively widening AIR gap between PTC and FTC does not appear to reflect a purely biological phenomenon. Instead, these population-level changes are highly consistent with systematic reporting shifts and diagnostic thresholds introduced in successive international staging and histopathological classifications.

item.title: A study on the temporal network characteristics of early post-chemotherapy core symptoms in colorectal cancer patients based on ecological momentary assessment.
item.dc:creator: Lv Y, Xu L, Li M, Cai X, Ye L, Wang X, Wang X, Chen Y, Lu Y
item.description:
Authors: Lv Y, Xu L, Li M, Cai X, Ye L, Wang X, Wang X, Chen Y, Lu Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1942076
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43010921



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) often experience multiple concurrent symptoms during the early post-chemotherapy period, and both symptom severity and inter-symptom associations may change over time. Previous low-frequency assessments may not adequately capture short-term fluctuations. OBJECTIVE: To characterize the dynamic trajectories and network features of early symptoms in patients receiving postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for CRC and to identify candidate symptoms for enhanced monitoring. METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) was performed three times daily for seven consecutive days after infusion in the first and second chemotherapy cycles and covered 13 symptoms. Linear mixed-effects models characterized symptom trajectories, and a multilevel vector autoregressive (mlVAR) model estimated temporal and contemporaneous networks. Edge uncertainty, centrality stability, sensitivity analyses, and between-cycle differences were evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients contributed 4,134 valid assessments (completion rate, 89.5%). All 13 symptoms showed significant time effects. Fatigue, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sleep disturbance fluctuated, whereas numbness/tingling and depression showed cumulative trends. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea had comparatively high outgoing temporal associations. The strongest individual temporal edge was modest (standardized coefficient approximately 0.12). No statistically significant between-cycle differences were found in overall network structure or global strength. CONCLUSION: Early post-chemotherapy symptoms showed dynamic changes and a broadly comparable network structure across the first two cycles. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea may be candidates for enhanced monitoring and future intervention research; the observational findings do not establish causal effects or intervention efficacy.
